summary.intent: Complete UAT for phase 21 (BYO IPFS node support), verifying that a user-supplied Kubo node running in local Docker works as a custom pinning backend in the cipher-box app.
summary.outcome: All phase 21 UAT items passed: the storage tab correctly connected to the local Dockerized Kubo node, pins were verified on the BYO node independently, and results were documented and committed to .planning/phases/21-byo-ipfs-node-support/21-UAT.md.

repo: The BYO Kubo node target shifted from a static IP address to a local Docker container — connection config must point at the Docker-exposed port rather than a remote IP.
The storage tab save button has an explicit gating condition that prevents saves from firing unless preconditions are met; this condition is separate from the migration UI appearing.
Migration UI displays a pin count progress ('migrating: 0/39 pins') independently of whether the save action has actually been triggered.
A TEE worker service is part of the infrastructure; its URL and routes live in a separate workspace directory and are configured via environment variables.
Pin existence on the BYO node can be independently verified via the Kubo RPC API, which was used as a ground-truth check separate from the app UI.

code.finding: UAT results document for phase 21; created and committed during this session as the canonical record of manual verification.

workflow: Puppeteer was used for browser-driven UAT: navigating, filling forms, clicking, and evaluating JS in the page to inspect component state.
API server logs were checked in parallel with UI actions to confirm requests actually reached the backend — useful for diagnosing silent UI failures.
When a UI action appeared to do nothing, the correct next step was to read the component's save-button gating logic in source rather than assuming a network or server error.
Independent Kubo RPC verification (via Bash, outside the app) was used to confirm pin state as a definitive ground truth check.

friction: Save button was silently disabled due to a gating condition — the migration UI rendered (showing '0/39 pins') which made it look like the action had fired, but no API request was made, causing a confusing diagnostic loop.
TEE worker configuration was opaque — required grepping across multiple workspace directories and inspecting compose files to locate the actual URL and routes.
Initial Kubo node connection assumption (IP-based) was stale; had to re-probe Docker ports and CORS config at the start of the session.
open_items: 39 existing pins flagged in the migration UI — it is unclear from the transcript whether all were successfully migrated to the BYO node or if migration was only partially tested.
CORS configuration on the local Kubo Docker container was investigated but no confirmation appears in the transcript that it was validated end-to-end for all required origins.
TEE worker integration with BYO node flow was inspected but not explicitly UAT-verified in this session.
